data.body:
`_ExportScheduler` builds one independent `_ExporterLane` (and therefore one dedicated daemon worker thread) per entry in `exporters`, with no de-duplication by identity.

Before this PR, `WorkflowInsightPlugin._emit` called every exporter serially in a single `for exporter in self._exporters:` loop on one thread, so even a config that (accidentally or deliberately) listed the same `InsightExporter` instance twice still only ever called that instance's `render`/`export`/`flush` from one thread at a time. After this change, each occurrence of that instance gets its own lane with its own worker thread, so the same exporter object can now be invoked concurrently from two different threads (e.g. lane A calling `export()` while lane B calls `flush()` on the identical instance). Any exporter that isn't internally thread-safe — buffers writes, keeps a non-atomic counter, holds a single file/socket handle — can now corrupt state or raise, which is a regression versus the previously-safe behavior for that configuration.

Fix: de-duplicate lanes by exporter identity in `_ExportScheduler.__init__` (map duplicate `exporters` entries onto the same lane instead of creating a new one), or validate against duplicate exporter instances in `WorkflowInsightConfig`/`workflow_insight()`, and document the resulting one-thread-per-distinct-exporter-instance contract on `InsightExporter`.
